correctness.rationale: The quotient identity follows from congruence x≡y (mod 3). A rigorous two-branch Apéry formula follows by eliminating mixed pairs u+v=3m. Because -2k≡1 (mod m), the two adjacency inequalities eliminate every residue class except indices k and k+1; they allow exactly h=1 and h=1,2, respectively. All three proposed numbers are positive for k≥2. Standard Apéry calculations verify Frobenius and genus. Two independent finite approaches (shortest-path Apéry algorithm and direct quotient enumeration) agree on all tested parameters; the symbolic proof applies to all integers k≥2.

value.rationale: The object is the natural smallest nontrivial fixed denominator quotient of consecutive coprime generators. Identifying all isolated gaps is a structural problem motivated independently by quotient and isolated-gap literature. The exact three locations for every k reveal a uniform, non-obvious invariant of an infinite embedding-dimension-three family. The value is the complete natural-family invariant, not the contextual Frobenius/genus deductions.
